findings.evidence: Lines 49–51 prove exactly the generic argument via `Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp`; Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/UnderlyingMap.lean:234 contains the corresponding `IsDominant.of_comp` API.
findings.fix: First add `IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.of_comp (g) (h) [IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant (g ≫ h)]`, analogous to Mathlib's `IsDominant.of_comp`, then derive this instance using `f.toNormalization_fromNormalization`.
findings.issue: `isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_fromNormalization` duplicates the general fact that if `g ≫ h` is scheme-theoretically dominant, then `h` is; its proof uses only `h.ker ≤ (g ≫ h).ker` and the composite equality.

findings.evidence: Lines 73–79 use affineness only through `isQuasicoherent_pushforward_of_isAffineHom`; once the pushforward is quasicoherent, the new general cokernel instance applies without further assumptions.
findings.fix: State the result under `[QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]`, proving/reusing the qcqs pushforward theorem, and obtain the affine case by inference.
findings.issue: The quasicoherent cokernel instance assumes the unnecessarily strong `[IsAffineHom f]`; direct image of a quasicoherent sheaf along a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme morphism is quasicoherent.

summary: Two declarations are stated at unnecessarily specialized levels: dominance of the normalization map is an instance of a general composition fact, and quasicoherence of the quotient only needs the standard qcqs pushforward hypothesis.
